remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Painted 1929." Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks date 1929. Backing inscriptions date 1930. Dated 1929 on basis of inclusion in 1930 New York (An American Place) exhibition and Stieglitz–O'Keeffe correspondence. Either this or cat. no. 745 mentioned in *New York Times* (January 1932 exhibition review) as being in 1931–32 New York (An American Place) exhibition. Reproduced in *Studio* (June 1931); reproduced and titled *Trees by Camp at Bear Lake* in *American Artist* (June 1943). See cat. nos. 696–98, 745, 1851. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: A huge gray tree with no foliage, seen from below, shoots dramatically upwards through this narrow composition. Flanking the tree are several pine trees full of dark green needles. The scene is set against a burgundy-colored background.
title: Dead Tree Bear Lake Taos
